name: Bulk-Download & Anomalous-Access Alert

parameters.content:
## Bulk-Download & Anomalous-Access Alert

### How it works

This workflow has TWO independent parts on one canvas:

**A. Real-time anomaly alert (top row)**
Runs hourly. Pulls Google Drive access activity from Google Workspace's own admin audit log, counts how many files each user viewed/downloaded/printed in that hour, and immediately emails the firm admin if anyone crosses a bulk-download or access-burst threshold — with the user, the matters touched, and the volume. A per-user cooldown stops the same person from re-triggering an alert every single hour while still elevated.

**B. Weekly visibility digest (bottom row)**
Runs weekly, independently. Re-pulls the last 7 days of the same audit log and emails a plain summary of who accessed the most files firm-wide — sent every week regardless of whether anything crossed a threshold, so the firm always has visibility into normal access patterns, not just alarms.

**This only ever reads metadata — who accessed which file name and when — never document contents.** It cannot tell you what's inside a file, only that it was opened, downloaded, or printed. That's a deliberate boundary: this is security monitoring, not legal review (ABA Op. 512).

### Setup steps

- [ ] Set up the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) first — every alert's audit logging goes through it.
- [ ] In Google Workspace Admin Console, enable API access and grant a service account domain-wide delegation with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.reports.audit.readonly` scope (Super Admin required — this is the one non-trivial setup step here).
- [ ] Add that as a Google API (OAuth2) credential in n8n.
- [ ] Configure an SMTP credential for sending alert/digest emails.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: FIRM_NAME, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, SECURITY_ALERT_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID.
- [ ] Optionally tune BULK_DOWNLOAD_THRESHOLD (default 15/hour), ACCESS_BURST_THRESHOLD (default 40/hour), ALERT_COOLDOWN_HOURS (default 6), LOOKBACK_HOURS (default 1).
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

### Customization

The matter reference shown in alerts is extracted from the file name itself (matching a `YYYY-XX-###` pattern) — rename files without that pattern and they'll just show as 'Unmatched / General Files', which is still useful, just less specific. Adjust the MATTER_REF_PATTERN regex in 'Normalize Drive Access Event' if your firm uses a different matter numbering convention. Coverage today is Google Workspace only — Microsoft 365 / SharePoint audit log support is a natural extension (coming soon).

## Watch for bulk downloads and access bursts

Every hour, pulls Google Drive access activity, counts downloads/views per user, and checks two independent signals: volume over threshold, and access from an IP never seen from that user before. Either one emails the firm admin — with the matter, user, and volume. A per-user cooldown keeps it from re-alerting every hour while still elevated.

## Weekly access visibility digest — a second, independent branch

Re-reads the last 7 days of the same audit log and always sends a plain summary of firm-wide access activity, even when nothing crossed an alert threshold — visibility, not just alarms.

nodes.name: Check Google Drive Access Logs Hourly
nodes.notes: Runs every hour on the hour. Adjust the cron expression here if your firm wants a different polling cadence — the LOOKBACK_HOURS variable should match whatever you set.

nodes.name: Fetch Recent Drive Activity From Google Workspace
nodes.notes: Pulls the firm's Google Workspace Drive audit log (who viewed/downloaded/printed which file, and when) for the last LOOKBACK_HOURS. Needs a Google API (OAuth2) credential with domain-wide delegation and the admin.reports.audit.readonly scope — this is the one real setup step in this template; see the workflow doc sticky. Firms with over 1000 relevant events per hour will need pagination added (not built here — most solo/small firms won't hit this).

nodes.name: Split Out Drive Activity Records
nodes.notes: Breaks the audit log response into one item per access event, so each can be checked and counted individually.

nodes.name: Normalize Drive Access Event
nodes.notes: Extracts the user, the file, whether it was a download/print (higher risk) or just a view, and tries to recognize a matter reference in the file name.

nodes.name: Filter Access-Relevant Events
nodes.notes: Drops edits, creates, renames, and other non-access events — only views/downloads/prints count toward this hour's volume.

nodes.name: Aggregate Access Counts By User
nodes.notes: Runs once for the whole batch (not once per item) — turns the list of individual access events into one summary row per user for this hour.

nodes.name: Check For New Access Location
nodes.notes: A second, independent anomaly signal alongside the volume thresholds: flags when a user accesses Drive from an IP never seen from them before. The first hour a user is ever observed just builds their baseline silently -- nothing alerts until a genuinely new IP shows up after that.

nodes.name: Check Against Anomaly Thresholds
nodes.notes: The firm's actual alert thresholds live here (BULK_DOWNLOAD_THRESHOLD, ACCESS_BURST_THRESHOLD) as n8n Variables, plus a cooldown so one elevated user doesn't spam an email every hour.

nodes.name: Filter Users Needing An Alert
nodes.notes: Only users who just crossed a threshold and are off cooldown make it through to an actual email.

nodes.name: Build Anomalous Access Alert Email
nodes.notes: Writes the actual alert email content. SECURITY_ALERT_EMAIL is an optional n8n Variable if you want these routed somewhere different from general firm alerts (falls back to FIRM_EMAIL).

nodes.name: Log Anomalous Access Alert For Compliance Audit
nodes.notes: Logs the alert to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet via the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) — internal record-keeping only, not a client message. Its 'approved' result is deliberately ignored: this is an internal firm security safety net and must never be suppressible, same fire-and-forget pattern used for internal-only notifications elsewhere in this catalog (PAC-59/60/61/63/67/74).

nodes.name: Send Anomalous Access Alert Email
nodes.notes: Sends the actual alert to the firm admin. Uses the FIRM_FROM_EMAIL variable as sender and the SMTP credential configured on this node.

nodes.name: Send Weekly Access Pattern Summary
nodes.notes: Runs weekly, Monday 8am by default — adjust the cron expression if a different day/time suits your firm.

nodes.name: Fetch Weekly Drive Activity From Google Workspace
nodes.notes: Same Google Workspace Drive audit log as the hourly branch, just pulled over the trailing 7 days instead of the last hour, for a firm-wide visibility digest rather than a threshold alert.

nodes.name: Split Out Weekly Activity Records
nodes.notes: Breaks the week's audit log response into one item per access event.

nodes.name: Normalize Weekly Access Event
nodes.notes: Same field extraction as the hourly branch's normalize step, applied to the week's events.

nodes.name: Filter Access-Relevant Events For Weekly Summary
nodes.notes: Same as the hourly branch: only views/downloads/prints count.

nodes.name: Aggregate Weekly Access By User
nodes.notes: Runs once for the whole batch -- produces a single firm-wide summary row, not one row per event.

nodes.name: Build Weekly Access Pattern Summary Email
nodes.notes: Explicitly sends a 'no activity this week' message rather than an empty table when the firm had zero Drive events.

nodes.name: Log Weekly Access Summary For Compliance Audit
nodes.notes: Same fire-and-forget audit logging as the hourly branch's guardrail call — internal record-keeping only.

nodes.name: Send Weekly Access Pattern Summary Email
nodes.notes: Sends the weekly digest to the same recipient as the hourly alert.

main.node: Fetch Recent Drive Activity From Google Workspace
Log Anomalous Access Alert For Compliance Audit
Fetch Weekly Drive Activity From Google Workspace
Filter Access-Relevant Events For Weekly Summary
Build Weekly Access Pattern Summary Email
Log Weekly Access Summary For Compliance Audit
Send Weekly Access Pattern Summary Email

description: Runs on two independent schedules. Hourly: pulls Google Workspace Drive access activity, counts views/downloads/prints per user, and emails the firm admin the moment anyone crosses a bulk-download or access-burst threshold, with a per-user cooldown so the same person doesn't re-trigger every hour. Weekly (separate): re-reads the last 7 days of the same audit log and always sends a firm-wide access summary for visibility. Reads metadata only -- who accessed which file name and when -- never document contents (ABA Op. 512). Replaces enterprise SIEM/DLP tools and manual log review.
